questions.question: During a bus ride, what should happen to the aisle?

options.text: Carry-on bags may be kept in the aisle.
Passengers may sit in the aisle.
The aisle must stay clear of objects.
Items can be in the aisle if passengers can step over them easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: The aisle must stay clear of objects.
questions.explanation: Do not leave carry-on bags in doorways or aisles. Nothing should be in the aisle that could make someone trip. Store bags safely to prevent damage.

questions.question: Tanks have high centers of gravity. This means:
questions.correctAnswerText: They roll over easily.
questions.explanation: Tanks have high centers of gravity, which makes them at risk of rolling over.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless you need to run the engine to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening the fill hole and keep it grounded until after closing the fill hole.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: Driving with hanging meat in a trailer is challenging because:

options.text: It is not safe during summer months.
Animals are attracted to the smell.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable. It has a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading a tank divided by bulkheads, equal weight distribution is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Some tanks have bulkheads that divide them into smaller sections. When loading or unloading, distribute weight evenly. Do not put too much weight on one end of the tank.

questions.question: Manhole covers should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Closed while driving the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle before driving. Never drive a tank vehicle with open valves or open manhole covers.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed, except during loading and unloading.

questions.question: A bus should be refueled:

options.text: In a closed building while passengers are on board.
Anywhere while passengers are on board.
Without passengers, unless it is absolutely necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Without passengers, unless it is absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely unavoidable. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside a closed building.

questions.question: An underloaded front axle:

options.text: Is good because front axles are weaker than other axles.
Should be avoided because it causes steering problems.
Should be avoided because it wastes fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it causes steering problems.
questions.explanation: Too little weight on the front axle can make it hard to steer safely. Pay attention to weight distribution when loading cargo.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Always feel the doors first to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from any building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, park at least 300 feet away from buildings, bridges, tunnels, places where people gather, and open fires.

questions.question: What is outage?

options.text: Only a concern in warm weather.
Something you must consider when filling a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something you must consider when filling a tank vehicle.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand when they get warmer. You must leave space in the tank for this expansion. This space is called outage. Different liquids need different amounts of outage.

questions.question: During an inspection, the most important thing to check on a tank vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: Check for leaks first. Carrying gas or liquid in a leaking tank is illegal.

questions.question: Containerized loads are used when:

options.text: The cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
The cargo has been or will be transported by train.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight is carried by train or ship. The driver should check that containers do not exceed weight limits, even though the contents cannot be inspected.

questions.question: As a truck driver with a load, you are NOT responsible for:

options.text: Knowing all fire department phone numbers along your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing all fire department phone numbers along your route.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for inspecting your cargo, checking for overloading or poor weight balance, ensuring cargo is properly secured, and making sure cargo does not block your view or emergency equipment access. You are not required to know fire department phone numbers along your route.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials shipping paper has a "G" in Column 1, what else must be included?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means the name in Column 2 is a generic name. Generic names must be paired with a technical name.

questions.question: Liquid surges are strongest in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Unbaffled tanks.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have barriers that stop liquid from moving forward and backward. Unbaffled tanks do not have these barriers, so surges are strongest in unbaffled tanks.

questions.question: A posted speed limit for cars:

options.text: May be too fast for buses.
May be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: Speed limits safe for cars may be too fast for buses, especially on curves. Be extra careful on wet or snowy roads.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, always use at least two tie-downs, regardless of cargo size.
